The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Planning
Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular Meetings are held on the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays of every month.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Clerk’s
Office at (626) 300-0705 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall, 2200
Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive and the Recreation Department,
1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s Website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Design Review Committee on any item of interest to the public, before or during the Design Review
Committee’s consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Design Review
Committee.

 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA – FEBRUARY 6, 2019  PAGE 3 OF 3

OPEN FORUM

This is an opportunity for future applicants to informally present preliminary design concepts for
feedback from members of the DRC. Comments received are based on members not having visited the
site and neighborhood. Therefore, positive comments should not be perceived as preliminary approval
of a project but rather as a tool in facilitating a project through the Design Review process. No more than
two DRC members may participate in Open Forum discussions. Applications that have been heard by
the DRC may not be discussed during Open Forum.

PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED

All public writings distributed by the City of San Marino to at least a majority of the Design Review
Committee regarding any item on this agenda will be made available at the Public Counter at City Hall
located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California.

ADJOURNMENT

The San Marino Design Review Committee will adjourn to the next regular meeting to be held on
Wednesday, February 20, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 2200 Huntington Drive,
San Marino, California.

APPEALS

There is a fifteen day appeal period for all applications. All appeals should be filed with the Planning
and Building Department. Please contact the Planning and Building Department for further information.
   City of San Marino

SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC18-85
  1539 OAK GROVE AVE., (RYAN/EPT DESIGN)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct front yard pilasters with lighting.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to CEQA
Guidelines Section 15303e because the project involves accessory structures.

PROJECT HISTORY

February 6, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
March 23, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve - 7
Object - 0
No response – 4

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

San Marino City Code Section 23.13.04G identifies separate design review findings relating to the
approval of fence, gates, walls and pilasters. It also states that the Design Review Committee may
reduce the maximum permitted height, increase the minimum required setback and decrease the maxi-
mum permitted opacity of any fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall located in the front yard.

The Design Review Committee may not reduce the maximum permitted height, increase the minimum
required setback or decrease the maximum permitted opacity of any fence, gate, yard wall or retaining
wall located in a side yard adjacent to a street; except, that the Design Review Committee or Commis-
 sion can increase the minimum setback for a gate providing access to a driveway in order to protect pe-
destrian or vehicular traffic.

The DRC shall approve the application for the pilasters with lighting fixtures in the front yard if it finds
all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall is architecturally com-
  patible with the existing residence.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The brick pilasters are architecturally compatible with the home as the same material
  is found on the exterior of the home. The lighting fixture style is traditional and the brass materi-
  al complements the pilasters and the home.

  2. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall is consistent with the
  size and location of fences, gates, pilasters, yard walls and retaining walls on the block on
  which the property is located.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  The Municipal Code defines Block as the property abutting on one side of a street and lying be-
  tween the two (2) nearest intersecting or intercepting streets or between the termination of such
  street and the nearest intersecting or intercepting street.

  Comments: The subject property is an interior lot along the north side of Oak Grove Avenue.
  There are pilasters and lighting found adjacent to the front property line along the subject Block.
  However, staff was unable to locate a pilaster or lighting fixture at the front of a structure, thus
  staff is unable to support the proposed pilaster near the entry walkway.

  3. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall preserves site lines and
  is otherwise located in a manner not to create a hazard to pedestrian or vehicular traffic.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE
  Comment: The pilasters with lighting along the front property line provide adequate setback and
  they are of a size and height that will not cause a hazardous condition to pedestrian or vehicular
  traffic.
    City of San Marino

SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC17-39
  860 ORLANDO RD., (LANGTON INVESTMENT CORP.)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a motorized driveway gate, fencing and pilasters with lighting in the
front yard.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to CEQA
Guidelines Section 15303e because the project involves accessory structures.

PROJECT HISTORY

February 6, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
March 23, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve - 6
Object - 0
No response – 5

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

San Marino City Code Section 23.13.04G identifies separate design review findings relating to the
approval of fence, gates, walls and pilasters. It also states that the Design Review Committee may
reduce the maximum permitted height, increase the minimum required setback and decrease the maxi-
mum permitted opacity of any fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall located in the front yard.

The Design Review Committee may not reduce the maximum permitted height, increase the minimum
required setback or decrease the maximum permitted opacity of any fence, gate, yard wall or retaining
 wall located in a side yard adjacent to a street; except, that the Design Review Committee or Commis-
sion can increase the minimum setback for a gate providing access to a driveway in order to protect pe-
destrian or vehicular traffic.

The DRC shall approve the application for the pilasters with lighting fixtures in the front yard if it finds
all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall is architecturally com-
  patible with the existing residence.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comment: The material and color of the pilasters, fencing, driveway gate and lighting fixture are
  compatible with the architectural elements exhibit on the residence.

  2. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall is consistent with the
  size and location of fences, gates, pilasters, yard walls and retaining walls on the block on
  which the property is located.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  The Municipal Code defines Block as the property abutting on one side of a street and lying be-
  tween the two (2) nearest intersecting or intercepting streets or between the termination of such
  street and the nearest intersecting or intercepting street.

  Comments: The subject property is one of two properties fronting on the Orlando Road based on
  the Block definition. The other property for comparison purpose is 870 Orlando Road which is
  improved with front yard pilasters and lighting fixtures. Staff can support the size and location of
  the fencing and the pilasters with lighting fixtures. Staff is unable to making the finding for a
  driveway gate as the only adjacent property on the Block is not improved with one.

  3. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall preserves site lines and
  is otherwise located in a manner not to create a hazard to pedestrian or vehicular traffic.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE
  Comments: The fencing is located behind existing hedges or matured landscaping and the drive-
  way gate is setback sufficiently to accommodate a full-size sedan without interrupting oncoming
  traffic. There is no sidewalk on both sides of Orlando Road west of Cameron Drive, thus pedes-
  trian traffic is very limited and there is adequate (16 feet from property line) setback to avoid
  visual clearance issue for drivers.

SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC18-67
  2195 ORLANDO RD., (XU/SLSD)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a one-story addition and remodel, construct a street-facing gate and
fencing.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to CEQA
Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) for fxisting facilities and Section 15303e for accessory structures.

PROJECT HISTORY

February 6, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
March 23, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve - 5
Object - 0
No response – 10

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS – ADDITION

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application if it
finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE
   Comments: The proposed one-story addition involves converting a portion (167 square feet) of
  the existing four-car garage into living area (Bedroom #4), expanding the garage to the west and
  expanding Bedroom and Bathroom #1. The most noticeable change to the structure would be the
  new garage doors and that one of the two garage doors will be 9-foot wide instead of the current
  configuration as shown on Sheet 8. The addition project minimally alters the building massing
  and bulk. The structure remains compatible with other two-story structures within the legal
  neighborhood.

  2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner which balances
  the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on contiguous properties with the
  reasonable expectations of the applicants to develop their property within the restrictions
  of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The addition areas are located on the first floor and will not provide direct sightlines
  into neighbor’s structure. Staff does not see any potential privacy issues or concerns associated
  with this project.

  3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing building
  which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The addition provides matching roof slope, roof eaves, and french doors. The project
  is well integrated with the existing structure and it will maintain the architectural characteristics
  of the structure.

  4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: Exterior colors, materials, and finishes will match existing and will be consistent
  throughout the building, except for the new wood windows. The project provides five new wood
  windows on the first floor, staff recommends that the new wood windows have the same
  bullnose treatment and grids (see Sheet 13, Detail 1) as the existing steel windows.

  The project includes re-roofing the structure with a City’s Pre-Approved roofing material (Boral,
  Cedarlite simulated roof tiles). New exterior lighting fixtures are provided where it is required by
  Building Codes and staff does not anticipate lighting pollution resulting from these fixtures.

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS – FENCING/GATE

San Marino City Code Section 23.13.04G identifies separate design review findings relating to the
approval of fence, gates, walls and pilasters. It also states that the Design Review Committee may
reduce the maximum permitted height, increase the minimum required setback and decrease the maxi-
mum permitted opacity of any fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall located in the front yard.
 The Design Review Committee may not reduce the maximum permitted height, increase the minimum
required setback or decrease the maximum permitted opacity of any fence, gate, yard wall or retaining
wall located in a side yard adjacent to a street; except, that the Design Review Committee or Commis-
sion can increase the minimum setback for a gate providing access to a driveway in order to protect pe-
destrian or vehicular traffic.

The DRC shall approve the application for the pilasters with lighting fixtures in the front yard if it finds
all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall is architecturally com-
  patible with the existing residence.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The material and color of the fencing and gate are architecturally compatible with the
  residnece. The driveway gate design is very similar to the side yard gate facing Orlando Road.

  2. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall is consistent with the
  size and location of fences, gates, pilasters, yard walls and retaining walls on the block on
  which the property is located.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  The Municipal Code defines Block as the property abutting on one side of a street and lying be-
  tween the two (2) nearest intersecting or intercepting streets or between the termination of such
  street and the nearest intersecting or intercepting street.

  Comments: The proposed driveway gate is intended to replace an existing gate at the same loca-
  tion. Unlike the existing driveway gate which has a solid appearance due to the mesh panel, the
  new driveway gate is a see-through picket gate with a bottom kick-plate. Staff finds the gate de-
  sign to be more compatible with the neighbor’s gate. Staff recommends using the same see-
  through picket design for the fencing that are identified by keynote #11 on the Enlarged Gate
  Plan on Sheet 11. The adjacent corner lot, 2170 Lombardy Road, has a driveway gate that is
  much closer to the structure and provide a greater setback from the side street as compared to the
  proposed driveway gate location.

  3. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall preserves site lines and
  is otherwise located in a manner not to create a hazard to pedestrian or vehicular traffic.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE
  Comment: The motorized driveway gate allows drivers to open the gate in advance to reduce the
  time that vehicles are blocking pedestrian traffic while waiting to gain access onto the property.
  The low hedges near the existing call box and the see-through gate design helps with visibility
  when a vehicle is approaching the gate from inside the property.
               City of San Marino

SUBJECT:  CONSIDERATION OF BORAL MADERA ROOF TILES PRODUCT
  FOR THE PRE-APPROVED ROOF MATERIALS COLORS AND
  APPLICATION LIST

BACKGROUND

Mr. Neal Gochman, Territory Manager for the Boral Roofing company, requests that the DRC consider
recommending the Boral Madera 900 simulated wood shake tiles product to the Planning Commission
for inclusion on the City’s Pre-Approved Roof Materials Colors and Application List.

The Boral Madera 900 product is manufactured by the Boral Roofing company, it is a simulated wood
shake product that shares the same production mold as the Boral Cedarlite product currently on the
City’s Pre-Approved Roof Materials Colors and Application List. Mr. Gochman will be at the meeting
to provide a presentation, show product samples, and answer questions about the product and its differ-
ences from the Cedarlite product that is installed throughout the City.

The Madera 900 simulated wood shake tiles product was before the DRC in October 2018 as modifica-
tions to replace the original Boral Cedarlite product previously approved on two new homes at 1221 Ro-
anoke Road (Vintage Wood color) and 2735 Canterbury Road (Autumnwood color).

The Madera 900 product is also installed at the following addresses:
  1. 1285 San Gabriel Blvd., San Marino, in Elkwood color
  2. 1304 San Carlos Rd., Arcadia, in Silverwood color
  3. 900 Monte Verde Dr., Arcadia, in Silverwood color
  4. 1409 San Carlos Rd., Arcadia, in Ironwood color
  5. 415 Magellan Rd., Arcadia, in Ironwood color
  6. 1115 Paloma Dr., Arcadia, in Autumnwood color
  7. 948 Hugo Reid Dr., Arcadia, in Autumnwood color

In reviewing a new roof material, the DRC may recommend conditions or requirements, such as color,
style of structure, or installation details. In addition to reviewing the appearance of the material, the
Committee should consider the following elements:
 1. Fire, wind and/or earthquake safety;
2. Structural integrity;
3. The extent the roof is exposed to public view or view by neighbors; and
4. The ability of the proposed roofing material to successfully dispose of rainwater.

Staff recommends the Committee hear the presentation by Mr. Gochman and consider the Madera 900
product with similar restrictions as the Cedarlite product that is currently on the List.
